info.title: Codebattle Public API
info.description: Narrow, me-centric API for bots, CLIs and devices. Every request needs a personal token (Settings → API tokens): `Authorization: Bearer cbp_...`. Objects you are not related to answer 404. Limits are per user: 60 requests/min, 5 games/min and 30/day, 5 tournaments/day, at most 3 unfinished API-created tournaments. In v1 only additive changes happen. Human and LLM-friendly docs: https://codebattle.hexlet.io/api-docs (Markdown: /api-docs.md).

Player.description: A person: you (`GET /me`), an online user, a game player, an invite's creator or recipient. Those objects extend it.

lang.description: Language of the player's editor in this game

result.description: `null` until the player's game is decided

result_percent.description: Hidden for opponents while the game is live

ends_at.description: starts_at + timeout_seconds: when the game times out

task.description: `null` while the game waits for an opponent, unless it is your game

visibility.description: `hidden` tasks are listed only for their creator

grade.description: `open` for user tournaments; season grades for official ones

starts_at.description: In the future, at most 30 days ahead

direction.description: `incoming`: you are the recipient and can accept

task_id.description: Task chosen by the creator, if any

state.description: The busiest of the user's open tabs

url.description: Game or tournament the user is on, if any

NotFound.description: Not found or not related to you

ValidationFailed.description: Invalid parameters; unknown fields are rejected

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The body is not sent as application/json

get.description: Who the token belongs to. A cheap way to check that a token works.

get.summary: Current live game (null if none). Count down with ends_at - server_time.
get.description: Your live game, or `null`: the one you are playing, or one you created that still waits for an opponent (`state: waiting_opponent`). Poll it (every few seconds is fine) to notice a game started from the web or by a tournament. Compute the remaining time as `ends_at - server_time`, not against your own clock.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` from the previous page: returns games with a smaller id.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only games started at or after this moment. ISO 8601 date (`2026-10-01`, midnight UTC) or datetime.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only games started before this moment. ISO 8601 date or datetime.

get.description: Finished games (`game_over` or `timeout`), 50 per page, newest first. Pagination is keyset-based: `next_cursor` is the id of the last game on the page; pass it back as `cursor` to get the next, older page. `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. `from`/`to` narrow the result by game start time and combine with `cursor`.

get.summary: Tournaments I created, moderate or play
get.description: Up to 50 tournaments you created, moderate or joined as a player, newest first.

get.summary: My pending invites, incoming and outgoing
get.description: Pending invites where you are the creator or the recipient. Supports long polling instead of frequent polls: pass `wait` (seconds, up to 30) and the `version` from your previous response. If the list already differs from that version the answer is immediate; otherwise the request is held until an invite is created, accepted or canceled, or until `wait` runs out, and then returns the current list. Loop on it to react to invites within a second with about two requests a minute. An accepted invite leaves the list; the creator finds the game via `GET /me/active_game`.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Hold the request up to this many seconds (0..30) while nothing changes.

version.description: Changes whenever the list changes; pass it back with `wait`

get.summary: Live stream of everything that happens to you (SSE)
get.description: A Server-Sent Events stream: one request that stays open. It starts with `hello` (your current state: active game, pending invites, unfinished tournaments), then sends one event per change: invites, your games, tournaments you play in or run. A `: ping` comment comes every 15 seconds. The server closes the stream after an hour with a `bye` event; reconnect and you get a fresh `hello`. At most 2 open streams per user. See **Event stream** above for every event and client examples.

200.description: An open event stream; see the Event stream section for every event

text/event-stream.example:
retry: 3000

id: 1791702000000
event: hello
data: {"user":{"id":42,"name":"ada",...},"active_game":null,"invites":[],"tournaments":[],"server_time":"2026-10-11T07:00:00Z"}

id: 1791702012345
event: invite.created
data: {"invite":{"id":9001,"direction":"incoming","creator":{"id":77,"name":"grace",...},...},"server_time":"2026-10-11T07:00:12Z"}

: ping

id: 1791702020000
event: game.started
data: {"game":{"id":324274,"state":"playing","url":"https://codebattle.hexlet.io/games/324274",...},"server_time":"2026-10-11T07:00:20Z"}

get.summary: Public upcoming and active tournaments for the next 14 days
get.description: Public tournaments that start between 1 day ago and 14 days ahead and are not finished yet: what the lobby shows as upcoming. For everything running right now use `GET /tournaments/live`.

get.summary: Tournaments running now or open for joining
get.description: Tournaments in `waiting_participants` or `active` state regardless of `starts_at`: all public ones plus private ones you created, moderate or play in. Newest first, at most 100.

post.summary: Create a private tournament (always grade open, tasks by level)

starts_at.description: In the future, at most 30 days ahead

post.description: Creates a private (`access_type: token`) tournament of grade `open`; tasks are picked by `level`. Share `invite_url` with players. Quota: 5 per day and at most 3 unfinished API-created tournaments.

get.summary: Tournament card: related to you, or public and scheduled
get.description: Works for tournaments related to you and for public ones. The creator and moderators also get `access_token` and `invite_url`.

patch.summary: Edit your tournament before it starts

starts_at.description: In the future, at most 30 days ahead

patch.description: Only the fields you send change. Allowed while the tournament is `upcoming` or `waiting_participants`.

get.summary: Ranking: full and paginated for the creator/moderators, top 20 plus your row for participants
get.description: The creator and moderators get the full ranking with `page` / `page_size` (max 100). Participants get the top 20 and their own row in `me`.

post.description: Starts your tournament now with the players who have joined.
Cancels your tournament and finishes its games.

get.description: Public active tasks plus your own, ordered by level and name. Use an `id` or `name` from here in `POST /games` or `POST /invites`.

parameters.name: tags
parameters.description: Comma-separated; tasks having any of these tags.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the task name.

get.description: What the lobby shows: games being played and games waiting for an opponent (usually a few Codebot games are waiting), newest first. Tournament games and other people's link games are not listed. Pass `state=waiting_opponent` for just the games you can join, then join one with `POST /games/{id}/join`; their task stays hidden until someone joins. Changes often; poll every 10–30 seconds.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only games in this state: `waiting_opponent` (open to join) or `playing`.

post.summary: Create a game: against a bot, or waiting for an opponent who joins by link

join_url.description: For `opponent: link`: the page to send your opponent

level.description: Required unless `task_id` or `task_name` is given; with a task it must equal the task's level.

task_id.description: Play this task (from `GET /tasks`). Pass this or `task_name`; without both a random task of `level` is picked.

post.description: `opponent: bot` starts the game immediately against Codebot. `opponent: link` creates a hidden game waiting for an opponent; send them `join_url`. Pick the task with `task_id` or `task_name` (see `GET /tasks`), or let the server pick a random one of `level`. Only tasks you may play are accepted: public ones and your own; any other answers 422 `no such task`. You can have only one active game at a time. Quota: 5 games per minute, 30 per day.

post.summary: Join a game that waits for an opponent
post.description: Joins a game from `GET /games/live?state=waiting_opponent`, or a `link` game whose id someone shared with you. The game starts at once; open its `url`. A failed join answers 422 `validation_failed` with `details.reason`: `not_waiting_opponent` (the game already started), `already_in_a_game` (you play another game: `details.active_game_id`; finish it or `POST /games/{id}/cancel` it if it still waits) or `already_joined` (you are already a player of this game).

post.summary: Cancel your game that waits for an opponent
post.description: Only a game in `waiting_opponent` state can be canceled.

post.summary: Invite a user to a game
post.description: Sends an invite that the recipient sees in the lobby and in `GET /me/invites`. One pending invite per pair of users.

recipient_id.description: Whom to invite. Pass this or `recipient_name`.

recipient_name.description: Exact user name, handy for voice commands

task_id.description: Play this task (from `GET /tasks`). Pass this or `task_name`; without both a random task of `level` is picked.

post.summary: Accept an invite sent to you
post.description: Starts the game for both players; the response has `game_id` and `game_url`. Fails with `422` if one of you is already in a game (the invite is then dropped).
The recipient declines, the creator withdraws. Only pending invites.

get.description: Registered users with codebattle open right now, highest rating first, with what they are doing. Changes slowly: polling every 30–60 seconds is plenty.
